title: Dharmottara's Mirage
summary: About twelve centuries before Gettier, the Indian Buddhist philosopher Dharmottara (c. 770 CE) described a traveller in the desert, looking for water, who sees a shimmering blue expanse ahead and believes there is water there. It is a mirage. But when he reaches the place, there is water after all, hidden under a rock. Did he know there was water there? His belief was true, and it was reasonable, but it was not the water that made him believe it. Such cases were argued over for centuries in Indian and Tibetan philosophy.
citations: Dharmottara (c. 770 CE), as discussed in Georges B. J. Dreyfus, Recognizing Reality: Dharmakīrti's Philosophy and Its Tibetan Interpretations (SUNY Press, 1997)
Edmund L. Gettier, "Is Justified True Belief Knowledge?", Analysis 23(6) (1963): 121–123
Jonathan Jenkins Ichikawa and Matthias Steup, "The Analysis of Knowledge," Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy: https://plato.stanford.edu/entries/knowledge-analysis/
